title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 9 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Roy Lopez left with a foot/ankle injury, Michael Wilson is carrying a heavy snap load, and Gardner Minshew's offense scored only 3 points in a sloppy loss at Seattle.
summary: LaFleur opened by saying Roy Lopez left with a foot/ankle injury and did not return, and that everyone else was fine. He spent most of the session blaming the offense's operation: slow getting in and out of the huddle, late play calls, and a lack of calm. He took responsibility for getting plays in faster. He said Michael Wilson is a warrior, but his heavy snap count means the staff must find faster substitution and personnel methods. The run game managed only 50 yards on 2.8 per carry, with tackles for loss in the red zone, and third downs in the first half hurt. He defended Gardner Minshew, calling the failure collective, and refused to blame young receivers or injuries. He said Kei'Trel Clark is doing a good job at nickel, which explains why Garrett Williams played only one snap, but he said Williams will get another opportunity. He also cited costly defensive penalties, including three offsides, and special teams errors. He dismissed a sideline spat between Josh Sweat and Darius Robinson as brotherly. He said the team needs to get healthy by taking care of itself in practice.

Roy Lopez and a player who sounds like center Hjalte Froholdt (the concussion protocol) will be known more as the week goes on. LaFleur praised Will Johnson and Jalen Brooks for playing through serious injuries, saying Brooks has a shattered arm. He said the receiver room is thin, calling it a chance for others to show what they can do, but named no replacements. If Minshew is out, he expects little change in the scheme with Carson, because the system is the same and both quarterbacks like it. He said the offense has had too many moving parts and not enough continuity, and he blamed himself for not stabilizing it after the loss to Seattle. The pre-snap operation, with substitutions and getting in and out of the huddle, and the in-play execution were both well short of the standard. He said he leaves trade-deadline matters to Monty and the front office.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Jessie Bates III trade & Atlanta Falcons preparation for Kansas City Chiefs | Press Conference
headline: Falcons are trading safety Jessie Bates III to Jacksonville. DeMarcco Hellams is the next man up at safety, with Billy Bowman also in the mix.

He then addressed the Jessie Bates III trade, calling it a tough, business-driven decision that helps the team long term, and said he and the front office all agreed on it. He rejected the idea that Atlanta is punting on the season, pointing out that the Falcons have three wins like the rest of their division and are still in the thick of it. On replacing Bates, he refused to name one successor and said everyone has to step up, though he called DeMarcco Hellams the next man up and noted Billy Bowman played safety in college. He liked the quarterback's 50 yards of scrambling and said it is a regular part of that player's game. He declined to say whether a kicker will be added, saying they are counting on 'Nick'. He also said a player named 'James' had a good first start after time away and should see his workload increase as his back injury allows.

title: Jesse Minter on Injuries, Mini-Bye Week, Upcoming Trade Deadline

Newly acquired QB Jacoby Brissett is expected to hit the ground running and start Monday night, with practice shifted so he gets extra time. Joe Fagnano, who started while hurt, earned respect and will be ready if called on. Minter admitted the secondary, including Marlon Humphrey, has been inconsistent and that explosive plays are his top defensive concern. He said lineup changes will be decided player by player and respects veterans' track records but must look at the current results. Kyle Hamilton looks fairly good and Jaylinn Hawkins (illness) is expected back at practice. Rasheen Ali had a minor in-game issue, and Adam Randall is still 10-12 days from a decision. Lee Hunter played only 13 snaps because the defense used more four-down looks. Canales said Hunter is healthy and the staff needs a better way to get him on the field in those packages. title: Ben Johnson on Bears' late-game confidence | Press Conference
headline: Bears are on a bye after a sloppy 4-INT win over Tampa Bay; Johnson says the run game needs fixing, Kyle Monangai's return would help it, and he leaves the trade deadline open.
summary: Johnson called the win over Tampa Bay a great result even though the Bears were not at their best. He credited the defense, which forced five turnovers, blocked a punt and allowed only ten points. He singled out Devin Bush, who had one of his best games as a Bear, and Austin Booker, whose effort keeps improving. He put Caleb Williams' four interceptions down to missed coverage reads, failed attempts to throw the ball away, and pass protection that needed to be better. He also took blame as the play caller for not getting the offense back on track after a poor second and third quarter. Theo Benedet played every snap while fighting through an injury, and Johnson praised his toughness. The self-scout this bye week will focus on the run game, which has averaged more than four yards per carry in only three of nine games. Johnson said Kyle Monangai's return will make the running game better, though he did not give a timeline. On the trade deadline, he said GM Ryan Poles is evaluating the roster, there may be a move or two, and he is confident in the current group.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' Sunday night victory over Buccaneers: 'We found a way' | Press Conference
headline: Bears beat Tampa Bay 27-24 despite five turnovers; WR Luther Burden III is in concussion protocol, and Devin Bush Jr. and Jaylon Johnson stood out on defense.
summary: Ben Johnson praised the team for finding a way to win 27-24 despite five turnovers, calling Tampa Bay a good team. He said the offense started hot, cooled through the middle of the game, and then got into field goal range at the end. The defense, in his view, was the story, since it held up in four sudden-change situations before Tampa finally scored on the last one. He said the pressure Tampa brought was handled well early but not later, and he flagged third down (2 for 12) as a recurring problem. He singled out Jaylon Johnson's pick-six, a coverage call from the defensive coordinator, and a lead block by Montez Sweat. He called Devin Bush Jr.'s game possibly his best as a Bear. On Caleb Williams' interceptions, he hadn't yet talked with the QB and planned to do so the next day. He said his in-game message was to get back on the horse. He also liked the return game, with Kalif Raymond and Zavion Thomas making plays, and felt calm calling the final drive. Burden's concussion and a thumb injury were the two injuries he mentioned.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: November 9th, 2026
headline: Todd Monken won't name a Week 10 starting QB between Deshaun Watson (cleared from concussion protocol) and Shedeur Sanders, who impressed in his first extended action. Dylan Sampson out-snapped Quinshon Judkins on game script.
summary: Monken declined to name a starting quarterback for Sunday. He said the offensive staff hasn't met on it yet and that he doesn't expect the decision by Tuesday's game-plan install. He said Deshaun Watson looks healthy and is out of concussion protocol, and he rejected the idea that a player loses a job to injury. He praised Shedeur Sanders for composure, escaping the pocket, a clean operation and a big third-down conversion. He said the performance gave him more confidence in what he saw in the fall, but it didn't change his thinking. He also repeatedly blamed penalties, execution mistakes and slow starts for the team being 5-4, and he took responsibility for them. He defended his overtime choices (deferring, going for two), and noted the Browns have four straight home games after a bye.

title: HC Sean Payton following Denver’s Week 9 win: ‘We still have some work to do’
headline: Denver beat Carolina before the bye. Pat Bryant is back and impressed, RJ Harvey is due back soon, and Sean Payton wouldn't discuss RB roles after Jonah Coleman started.
summary: Sean Payton called the Week 9 win over Carolina a good one before the bye, with things to clean up. A key moment was a late, hard-to-see interception in the end zone by Devon Key, which Payton says was spotted from upstairs and challenged. Nik Bonitto made a huge play that fixed the team's ball-security problem. Payton said the offense's recent run of 30, 28 and 26 points is partly down to Denver using a lot more Buffalo nickel, and the team also has a new defensive coordinator. On the backfield, Jonah Coleman started and did well, and RJ Harvey will be back shortly. Payton refused to talk about running back depth, and said the run game wasn't good against a Buffalo front, with chunk plays coming more through the air. Denver went after the Panthers' practice-squad corners with a Delta go call, swapping in Marvin Mims Jr. and Troy Franklin on the second play and drawing a pass interference penalty. Pat Bryant returned and Payton praised his hands in traffic, football IQ and run after the catch. A couple of players got nicked up before the bye, apparently including a concussion. Payton likes his team but says there is still work to do. The bye plan is rest and treatment, then a jump start on Las Vegas. He called trade-deadline activity impossible to predict.

He said the pass protection was leaky early against a defensive front that wins with low leverage, and that the line adjusted too slowly before tightening up in the second half. title: Matt LaFleur after win vs. Patriots: 'That was a total team victory right there'
headline: Josh Jacobs fractured a finger and may struggle to grip the ball, so Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong could see more work. Jordan Love, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Savion Williams all drew praise after the 45-27 win.
summary: LaFleur called the win over the Patriots a total team victory, with the offense, defense and special teams all contributing. He said Golden, Watson and Savion Williams all had big nights, and called Williams' touchdown catch spectacular. The run game topped 100 yards against a stout defense, though LaFleur said the team is still far from a finished product. Josh Jacobs fractured a finger and had trouble gripping the ball. title: Shane Steichen: Week 9 recap, Colts vs. Cowboys
headline: Steichen says Tyler Warren needs to get more involved as he works back from a groin injury, while the run game was held in check by Dallas and the trade deadline (4:00 tomorrow) leaves roster questions open, including Daniel Jones.
summary: Steichen opened by saying the Colts must finish games and be at their best when it matters, and they failed to do so against Dallas. He declined to speculate on trade deadline matters, calling them organizational decisions, and said his focus is on preparing for the Miami Dolphins. He defended the aggressive third-and-8 call late in the game as a deliberate 'play ball' situation, since Dallas had all three timeouts and the aim was to get a first down and set up a winning field goal. On Tyler Warren, he said the tight end is still working back from a groin injury and the team needs to get him more involved this week and beyond. He credited Dallas for its run defense, which used true 3-4 looks, 3-4 under looks and mixed fronts; the Colts topped 100 rushing yards but were not efficient early, and he put it on the whole unit, especially up front. title: Coen on Acquisition of S Jessie Bates III, What Bates Brings to Locker Room | Press Conference

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Texans
headline: Justin Herbert hurt his left middle finger (possible fracture) after getting sacked 8 times in a 38-9 loss to Houston, and Cole Strange was benched, so Chargers offense risk is high.
summary: Harbaugh said the Chargers lost badly to the Texans, whom he credited for making incredible plays, including tight-coverage catches. He said the team will stay together and keep fighting, and he rejected the idea that the locker room could fracture. He said the offense can be fixed and framed it as a matter of making plays when opportunities arise. The team was poor on third down on both sides of the ball. Justin Herbert was sacked eight times, and Harbaugh said the staff made halftime adjustments and will keep working on protection. Cole Strange was benched at halftime, and Harbaugh said there is a chance someone else gets the starting job going forward. Herbert hurt his left middle finger after throwing a touchdown. Harbaugh said he made the call to pull him even though Herbert wanted to go back in, and the injury could be a fracture. A backup quarterback finished the game, and Harbaugh said he stayed poised and executed. Harbaugh also said it was good to see an explosive play end the touchdown drought, and he admitted that leaving tight end Charlie Kolar and Scott Matlock one-on-one against edge rushers is sometimes part of the design.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 11/8: "It’s on all of us. It starts with me”
headline: Rhamondre Stevenson left the loss to Green Bay and could not return, with no update on the injury; Drake Maye's four-turnover day and Christian Gonzalez's struggles drew criticism but no lineup changes.
summary: Vrabel took blame after a lopsided Week 9 loss to Green Bay that dropped New England to 5-4. On Drake Maye, he cited pressure, some Packers scheme and execution, and his own team's ball placement and decisions, and said he expects Maye to rebound. Rhamondre Stevenson came off and did not return, and Vrabel said he didn't know the extent of the injury and wouldn't speculate. He is troubled by a third straight slow start and said the team may change how it practices. He was frustrated by three pre-snap defensive penalties and had no fix yet, and he explained that he passed on a challenge because he got a report that the catch was good.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 9, 2026
headline: Eagles (2-7) head into the bye in self-scout mode with no concrete lineup or role news; Sirianni backed rookie T Markel Bell as 'solid' and dodged questions about staff changes and selling at the deadline.

He said the offense is the Eagles' offense rather than any one coordinator's, that elements from several coaches have been blended, and that the offense must be better. He denied making a rude gesture at fans, said no coaching staff changes were being discussed beyond the self-scout, and explained that his late postgame press conference was due to a player wanting to talk. Asked whether the 2-7 Eagles would be sellers at the trade deadline, he declined to engage and said his focus is righting the ship. No injury updates, depth chart changes or opponent info were given.

title: WATCH: The Mike McCarthy Press Conference Show presented by PNC (Week 10)
headline: Steelers (6-2) come off the bye with Pittman and Harmon close but not projected for Cincinnati; McCarthy says he must get DK Metcalf more involved, and Darnell Washington may see more red-zone work.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Recaps Week 9, Provides Injury Updates
headline: Drew Lock (oblique) is expected to start again with Jalen Milroe as the backup, Sam Darnold could return after the bye, and Quenton Nelson had surgery but is not on IR (week to week).

title: Shanahan Reflects on Dominant Win Over Raiders, Praises Defense’s Takeaways
headline: 49ers offense is healthy and rolling: McCaffrey is fine after the bye and Jordan Watkins is emerging at WR. Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) are unclear, and DT Gracen Halton is likely out for the season.
summary: Shanahan was happy with a complete win over the Raiders. The defense forced five second-half turnovers, including a pick-six by Jaden Dugger and a Renardo Green interception, after the team had struggled to create turnovers. The offense ran for 190 yards on 43 carries and did well on third down, with no punts. Shanahan said he had forgotten about Christian McCaffrey's injury from the previous game, because McCaffrey assured him before the bye that he would be fine. He praised Jordan Watkins as taking a huge step forward, and said Kaelon Black ran hard and Jordan James is still developing. Brock Purdy missed a few throws early but scored on every one of those drives, and Shanahan called his scrambling effective and spontaneous. On injuries, Green left with a back problem and Lenoir with a foot problem, and both need more evaluation. Halton broke his ankle and is expected to miss the rest of the year. title: Todd Bowles Discusses Trade Deadline Strategy | Press Conference
headline: Bowles says Bucky Irving's workload (on pace for ~315 carries) must be trimmed after the bye, while the passing game, Baker Mayfield, and rookie WR Ted Hurst remain works in progress.
summary: Bowles said the offense's biggest problems are turnovers, pass protection, penalties (five false starts) and receiver drops, and that the team regressed to where it was a month ago. He said the staff will use the bye week to examine Baker Mayfield's comfort with the play calls, the scheme, and his mechanics, and expects to make changes. He did not commit to a play-caller change. Bucky Irving is the bell cow, but Bowles doubts his frame can handle a 315-carry pace and said some carries will have to come off him. Rookie Ted Hurst played one snap after an early drop; Bowles said he is still learning the offense's nuances, and the team wants to get him the ball more. On Emeka Egbuka, he cited health as the main reason for the production drop and said the staff needs to design more plays for him. Cade Otton's target volume is up because defenses double the outside receivers and the tight end slips out for passes. Antoine Winfield Jr. left with an ankle injury of unknown severity, YaYa Diaby is hoped back for Detroit, and Jalen McMillan, still on IR after a knee procedure, is uncertain. On the trade deadline, Bowles said the team is listening both ways, and nothing is imminent.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cam Ward's strong game vs. Cincinnati gets Saleh's praise, but he warns of ups and downs. Tyjae Spears is 'ailing' and Tony Pollard and Michael Carter are covering at RB. Full injury news waits until Wednesday.
summary: Saleh held all injury updates until Wednesday, saying a few players coming off the bye need to be checked. title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/9/26
headline: Lucas Patrick is in the concussion protocol, so the line is shuffling for a short-week road game. Treylon Burks and Amik Robertson are trending toward playing Thursday, and Stefon Diggs is still a priority despite a quiet game.
summary: Quinn opened by saying the team has to turn the page quickly. He repeated that he is chasing consistent football for a full game and admitted he is tired of saying it. He said the offensive line and run game were not up to standard, and that three-and-outs in the third quarter cost them chances to run. He called third-down conversions and sustained drives the fix. Center Lucas Patrick is in the protocol, and Nick Allegretti and Matt Gulbin are the candidates to replace him. Amik Robertson's ankle improved and Treylon Burks is trending toward returning, with Tuesday as the key day. Quinn said he would not hesitate to make personnel changes if the evaluation points that way. He said there is no change to the trade-deadline approach after the loss. topics.detail: Quinn said the run game was not up to standard and the team needs more chances to run. He tied that to converting third downs and sustaining drives, not simply handing off more.
He was frustrated by two false starts (the center and the left tackle) after practicing cadences all week. He said the process was good and expects it to be fixed.
Asked about the opposing receiver's production against zone coverage, he said the answer is to speed up the rush with a fifth or sixth rusher. He said the pass rush was not getting home consistently.

He defended offensive coordinator David Blough as competitive and talented. He said fans don't see everything that goes into the calls. He said he is evaluating how to put people in the best spots and would not hesitate to make personnel changes if that is the problem.
Quinn said the loss changes nothing about the team's trade-deadline approach, and that calls and discussions are routine for GM Adam Peters and his staff.

He said the staff does a deep dive on every injury, including practice, training and fueling, plus recovery work by the performance staff. The receiver group started the year healthy, but Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown have all been hurt.
Quinn avoided one-game declarations but said the team needs the win Thursday against the division leaders and everyone in the building knows it.
